hockey_player.evidence: The figure holds a stick with a blade and has a helmeted head, but the complete lack of skates makes it look like a peg gliding on a flat base.

toy.evidence: The cylindrical body, spherical head, and simple sphere hands strongly convey a chunky peg-toy aesthetic, though the dark color obscures the volume.

answer.best_row: Bottom row, because the isolated figures against the white ice provide better contrast to read the silhouette and stick angle compared to the clustered top row.
changes: Add visible skates to the bottom of the cylinder to clarify the hockey theme.
Change the dark grey material to the intended deep blue or warm orange to improve contrast.
Increase the thickness of the stick shaft by 50% so it remains visible at downscaled sizes.
head 0.33 of height -> 0.40 to further emphasize the toy-like proportions.
worst: The absence of skates breaks the hockey player read, making it look like a generic board game peg.
The uniform dark grey color blends into its own shadows, flattening the forms.
At the downscaled size, the thin stick shaft becomes nearly invisible or reads as noise.
works: The cylindrical body and spherical head successfully establish a chunky, toy-like aesthetic.
The helmet visor shape is simple but effective at indicating the front of the head.
The simple sphere hands fit the toy style perfectly while clearly holding the stick.
